portable_bounds.integer_domain: JSON integer literal, 0 <= n <= 9007199254740991 (JS Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); no fractional or exponential form, no NaN/Infinity
portable_bounds.note: Package-local v0 self-imposed limits for bounded parsing only. Not a claim about ReceiptOS domain semantics -- ReceiptOS itself imposes no such limits.

collection_ref_derivation.escaping_rule: Every byte of the UTF-8 encoding of collection_id that is not one of the unreserved ASCII characters above is percent-encoded as %XX, uppercase hex, one escape per byte.
collection_ref_derivation.not_equivalent_to: Python's urllib.parse.quote(collection_id, safe="") with default settings. quote()'s always-safe set is only letters/digits/_.-~, so it percent-encodes ! * ' ( ), which encodeURIComponent does not. Confirmed empirically during design: quote() produces a%20b%27c%28d%29e%21f%2Ag%2Fh for the self-test input below, which is byte-different from the real encodeURIComponent output.

self_test.note: Deliberately outside the normative identifier_grammar -- exercises the escaping algorithm itself, not a claim that such identifiers are portable/normative for this package's matrix.

comparators.artifact_refs_and_collection_refs: String.prototype.localeCompare in the committed TS implementation (sortArtifactRefs / sortCollectionRefs) -- locale/ICU-dependent
comparators.checkpoint_entry_refs: plain codepoint order (< / >) for canonical ordering (sortEntryRefs); checkpoint_root itself uses STORED order, never re-sorted
comparators.portable_v0_substitute: Python sorted() (codepoint order) is used for all ref sorting in producer_reference.py and verify_output.py
comparators.agreement_scope: Proven to agree with the real, unmodified committed comparators only for the exact normative strings enumerated below -- this package makes no general Unicode/localeCompare portability claim. See the focused ReceiptOS test's comparator-agreement case, which sorts these exact strings both ways using the real sortArtifactRefs/sortCollectionRefs/sortEntryRefs functions.

applicability_rules.checkpoint_sequence: sequence must be a non-negative JSON integer
applicability_rules.checkpoint_continuation: sequence > 0 requires prev_checkpoint non-null (any non-null value)
applicability_rules.note: These document already-existing rules from createChroniclePortfolioV0 and validateChronicleCheckpointShape in the frozen chronicle-portfolio-v0.ts. This package changes none of them -- it only writes them down in prose/data reachable without reading TS source.

root_formulas.canonical_json: object keys sorted; array order preserved including duplicates; UTF-8; no Unicode normalization performed anywhere
excluded_from_every_preimage: schema on Collection/Portfolio (present on the object, absent from its own root preimage)
metadata (not used anywhere in this package's matrix)

topology.note: No producer-controlled filenames anywhere in this topology -- every name is fixed and normative, eliminating path traversal and Windows case-collision risk by construction rather than by runtime policy alone.

never_trusted_as_evidence: any classification the producer might claim
trust_boundary.note: producer_id/producer_version may never be read by verification logic -- extends the existing PORTABLE_EVIDENCE_ENVELOPE_NOTE.md principle (producer identity is provenance metadata, not proof truth) into the Chronicle domain.

reference_corpus.cross_check_note: Every root above was independently computed by producer_reference.py and cross-checked byte-for-byte against the real, unmodified computeChronicleCollectionRoot/computeChroniclePortfolioRoot/computeChronicleCheckpointRoot from src/receiptos/capsule/chronicle-portfolio-v0.ts during design -- confirmed identical.

fixture_set_recipe: Sorted member paths except manifest.json: <path>\t<file-sha256>\n concatenated UTF-8 then SHA-256.
